Messages.Author: Joshua Duffin
Messages.Body:
"Jeroen" <joen...@hotmail.com> wrote in message
news:5f0d2397.03112...@posting.google.com...

[re Capitalist]

> OK, it's probably not broken as in "changing the way the game is
> played"-broken, BUT the point is that the best Archtype has been given
> to a decktype that was already powerful enough.

The interesting thing (well, I find it interesting) is that it's the
best Archetype *because* it goes to the best decktype. Bleeding is the
easiest thing to succeed at -> bleed decks are in many ways the
strongest decks -> the bleed Archetype is the best one. It's kind of
self-reinforcing, if you see what I mean: when you make a similar card
for various strategies, the bleed one is inherently likely to be the
strongest, and then it may therefore make the bleed strategy even
stronger.

I do think that the countervailing force of "bleed already has so many
good cards that new ones have to compete for cardslots with them" has a
significant effect, though. Not that this necessarily excuses the
principle. After all, "weenie decks need no help" and one could easily
make the same argument for bleed decks. :-)

> The low-midcap Dem bleeder has been helped in so many ways by Black
> Hand: Midget, The Colonel, the card that lets you search a card from
> your library (name?), Gemini's Mirror and of course Capitalist.

The search card is Sibyl's Tongue and it's a !Malkavian-requiring
action. I think that card is interesting and potentially powerful, but
it's limited by both being an action (thus competing not only for
cardslots but also actions available, and slowing down your ability to
use the card you go get) and by costing an increasing amount of blood to
search multiple times (cost of the card is X, where X is the number of
Sibyl's Tongues already in your ash heap).

Josh

> >

True, although then you're no longer able to say "Capitalist removes
Zoe's disadvantage, you're now saying "Capitalism combined with Into
the Fire removes it", and I'm okay with that.

And with regards to the above comments about Zoe: Yes, you can regain
a blood through Night Moves. Without Night Moves (or some other card
to stealth her bleed), Capitalist doesn't really help at all. If you
were already putting Night Moves or other stealth cards in your deck
for Zoe, that means you weren't planning to have Zoe hunt in the first
place, but bleed bleed bleed. Yes, Capitalist/Into The Fire lets you
do 'Blood Doll/Night Moves' instead of how you would play 'Blood
Doll/I'll hunt cardlessly' on a similar vampire. Again, I'm totally
okay with Capitalist 'removing Zoe's disadvantage' in a fashion that
is only reliably effective by both Into the Fire and also the use of
even more cards beyond that.

Having to play a (at least) three-card combo to undo a vampire's
disadvantage is hardly a reason for concern or to claim it makes one
of the cards additionally powerful, to me.

-John Flournoy

That's just not why it's the most potent Archetype. All you need to
bleed successfully is have enough stealth. Every other archetype
requires something rather more than this though Guru is fairly close in
power. Creep Show relies entirely on the opponent to give you the blood
-and when you get the blood it's because of something you didn't really
want the opponent to do. Sociopath would need to trigger whenever you do
damage to another minion (once a turn/table-round) in order to be
equivalent.

I think it's a shame that all the archetypes are Sabbat-only.
